A customer who reports a wrong charge but can't yet name the invoice or line still gets the case now, with what they gave you. Quote the retrieved rule naming the owning team in `routing_rule`. Route by what the customer asks for, not by the topic: a request for a credit on charges you have explained follows the credit-request row, not the invoice-dispute row.

Use its named team and trigger; do not infer eligibility or choose a team from a product contact. Do not open a case for an informational question, an unavailable console field, or an unmet waiting-period trigger. In a resolved embeddings investigation for `rw-embed-3-large`, Redwood confirmed it counts with the model-native tokenizer, which can differ on Unicode normalization and whitespace. It counts the full text input, including leading or trailing spaces. Multiple inputs are counted individually after normalization, so batching alone shouldn’t increase the total.

## When a case is needed
Open a case only when the customer asks for something Support can't do in the conversation, or reports a problem the related pages don't explain. Answering a question needs no case.

- Answer, don't hand off: how billed tokens are counted (model-native tokenizer, full request payload), why retries and cancelled streams are billed, and why the Console lags a few minutes are covered in the related pages. If one of them explains what the customer sees, explain it and stop there, even if the customer calls it a bug or double billing.
- If an older page says something different from the current one, explain the current behaviour and which page is current. That needs no case, even if the customer asks to report the old page as a bug.
